label: Degree of act, degree of knowability and degree of knowing: primitive measures on one scale
term: degree of act, knowability and knowing (Lean `ComprehensionByMeasure.Measures`)
definition: PRIMITIVE measures on a degree scale Deg (a Mathlib Preorder: reflexive and transitive, not assumed total or antisymmetric). actDegree x: the degree to which x is in act, in being. knowability y: the degree to which y is knowable in itself, not to us (ST I q.12 a.1: a thing is knowable insofar as it is in act). KnowsAt x y d: x knows y with a knowing whose perfection is d. Maximality is Mathlib's IsTop (no degree on the scale exceeds it). Examples: a living thing is more in act than a stone (the grades of q.4 a.2); a mathematician who knows a theorem by its demonstration knows it at a higher degree than one who holds it on the authority of others (the example of q.12 a.7). Counterexamples: a degree of knowability is not a degree of being known (y may be knowable beyond every degree at which anyone knows it); a degree of knowing is not the number of things known. Distinguished from the Fourth Way comparative MoreIn esse (which relates beings and assigns no degree; no bridge between them is stated), from the homogeneous scale of the quarta via results (a preorder on beings, not on degrees), and from the propositional Veracity.Knows of NamingVeracityBatch1 (a relation to a proposition, not to a being).
note: Analyst primitives, attribution deferred; introduced to give the primitive COMPREHEND_1 (definition 4afe4ab4) a typed sibling COMPREHEND_2 from which the q.12 a.7 bridge 'No intellect that is not INFINITE_1 comprehends an INFINITE_1 being' is derived. No axiom constrains them: the four open premises of ComprehensionByMeasure (infinite act is maximal; knowable at least insofar as in act; non-INFINITE_1 act is not maximal; knowing within the knower's act) are the only constraints. Structural properties: only those of the Preorder. Commitment of the form: where something is INFINITE_1, InfiniteActIsMaximal needs a scale with a maximum (Control part 8: on a scale with no maximum it entails that nothing is INFINITE_1). Would be sourced by pinned readings of q.12 a.1, a.4 and a.7 (q.16 a.3 is pinned, claim 191c4ad9, and supports the knowability premise only as a comparative).
